transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
Flights are halted at airports across the U.S.
due to what the FAA calls "extraordinary circumstances
and reasons for safety."
The agency says that all departing traffic
will remain ground-stopped until further notice
and that inbound flights will be managed on a case-by-case basis.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy posted online
that the ground-stop was issued because of a "communication issue
impacting all route traffic control centers"
and that technicians are investigating.
The European Council president says diplomats from the U.K.,
France, Germany, Italy and Poland will go to Ukraine for peace talks.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky
wants more support from European allies.
He met with U.S. Envoy Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff yesterday in Dublin
after they met with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
While the Trump administration is raising hopes of a possible breakthrough,
Putin is sticking to his hard lines.
He still wants Ukraine to hand over territory Russia has not conquered
and says foreign peacekeepers in Ukraine would be considered a legitimate target.
Zelensky expressed frustration over the U.S.-controlled
Star Shield satellite connection being slowed down again.
He said Star Shield is vital to intercepting Russia's new jet-powered drones.
Putin called on Europe to end its support for Ukraine.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Cave.
The Supreme Court has agreed to consider President Trump's executive order
suspending asylum access at the southern border.
The Trump administration wants the high court to overturn lower court decisions
that found the ban unlawful.
Federal law allows people to seek asylum if they fear persecution,
but the executive branch decides whether to agrant it.
SpaceX is preparing a critical test launch of its massive Starship rocket this afternoon.
As NPR's Jeff Brumfield reports, this test will be important to the company's future.
Starship is the largest rocket ever built.
It might one day take humans to Mars, but first it's got to make SpaceX a lot of money.
The plan is to use the rocket to launch thousands of Starlink internet satellites
and further down the line orbital data centers.
The only way Starship can take all this stuff into space is if it can be quickly reused.
To that end, SpaceX intends to fly this test rocket back from orbit to its launch pad in Texas.
If all goes to plan, it will hover while two mechanical arms on the launch tower catch it.
Eventually, the company plans to simply gas up the rocket after it's caught and launch it again.
Jeff Brumfield, NPR News.
A tanker has struck a river cruise boat in New Orleans
with more than a hundred passengers on board leaving the boat on its side.
Rescues are underway on the Mississippi River.
Authorities have not yet released information on injuries or deaths.
Video from the scene shows the much larger tanker hitting the paddlewheel cruise boat,
which was docked at the time people were seen in the river in life jackets or standing near the railing
as the other side of the American heritage lists further into the water.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
The FBI says it has seized or restrained more than $1.2 billion of cryptocurrency reported stolen last month from Binance.
The theft of $6.3 billion from the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange is regarded as the biggest crypto heist in history.
The FBI has previously attributed it to a North Korean hacking group called Traitor Traitor.
The U.S. government and private sector have so far combined to freeze more than $2.7 billion of the stolen funds.
In Turkey, almost 200 countries are discussing how to limit emissions from fossil fuels
now that their current climate goal is out of reach, NPR's Lauren Summer reports.
It's 11 years ago now that countries agreed on a goal to stave off the most intense impacts of climate change.
Warming would be limited to 1.5 degrees Celsius, which is 2.7 degrees Fahrenheit.
Now, that goal is out of reach.
The planet has almost reached that level of warming, and countries continue to burn fossil fuels.
Discussions at the COP 31 climate summit are now focused on how much hotter it will get,
which affects extreme weather around the planet.
Despite the U.S. being one of the largest producers of greenhouse gas emissions,
the Trump administration is not participating in the talks.
Lauren Summer, NPR News.
Production of the Rubik's Cube is returning to its native Hungary.
Invented by Hungarian architect Erno Rubik in 1974, over half a billion units have been sold.
A new automated production line opened in Jaspa Rainy.
Rubik originally produced the design as the Magic Cube, and it gained popularity in the late 1970s.
By the early 1980s, it had become a global sensation.
The cube remains a cultural icon.
This is NPR News.

European diplomats from five countries to travel to Ukraine for peace talks; Zelensky seeks more support
Supreme Court agrees to consider Trump executive order suspending asylum access at southern border
SpaceX prepares test launch of Starship rocket, aiming to catch and reuse it at Texas pad
Tanker strikes river cruise boat on Mississippi River in New Orleans; passengers rescued, injuries unknown
FBI seizes or restrains over $1.2 billion of cryptocurrency stolen from Binance last month
